agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: To keep using the remaining passes on something specific, I'll first test a hypothesis that needs no pass. My readings described "dropped conditions": wrong setups that ignore part of the question. If that is a real failure type, wrong finished answers should leave out more of the question's numbers than correct finished answers do, even after controlling for difficulty. To control for that, I'll compare within problems the model got right in one pass and wrong in another, and also across all DEV answers matched by the number count of the question. A clear gap, say wrong answers missing 15+ points more of the question's numbers, would make "unused question quantities" a target. That target would be tracking which numbers are already used, a different mechanism from the fetch heads, which only read numbers. No gap closes the last setup hypothesis.

The block failed at the pair step only: pair_meta has one entry per pair (77), not one per text, so the index has to be j//2. The first two parts of the analysis are unaffected. I'll rerun with that fix. The hypothesis and the decision rule stay the same.

The dropped-number effect is real but small once difficulty is controlled. Overall, 35% of wrong finished answers leave out at least one question number, against 14% of correct ones. But within the same problem, correct answers use only 4.9 ± 2.6 points more of the question's numbers, well below the 15-point bar I set, and the gap in the matched bins is also a few points. Most of the raw difference reflects harder problems with more numbers. So "dropped conditions" exists but explains only a small part of the errors.

To see whether it is tied to a specific step, I'll use the original's reference-solution logprobs (fwd_3, no pass needed). I'll split question-number operands into first use of each number versus later reuse. If first uses are predicted much worse than reuses, the model has trouble deciding which unused quantity comes next, a used-number tracking failure that could be localised. If the two are similar, number selection is not a distinct weak point, and I'll close the dropped-conditions line.

First uses of question numbers are predicted only slightly worse than reuses (−0.71 vs −0.62 nats). The model does not have a specific problem choosing which unused quantity comes next, so I'm closing the dropped-conditions line.
